units.title: Image patches, vision encoders and visual-token counts, and resolution, context and compute cost
outcomes: Derive separate token counts for the vision encoder and the language decoder after merging and delimiters.
Implement rectangular patch extraction with an explicit flattening order and grid coordinates.
Budget resolution changes across vision attention, decoder context and cached state.
units.why: Patch extraction is already familiar from Patch embeddings and positional information. The research problem is tracking what survives preprocessing and compression, and which component pays for each token.

study.title: Qwen2-VL, arXiv:2409.12191v1
study.locator: Section 2.1, Naive Dynamic Resolution: 2D positions, adjacent 2 by 2 token compression and vision delimiters

focus: Count the processed image, not its original dimensions. Resizing, cropping and tiling change both evidence and token count.
For divisible dimensions and square patch width \(p\), the vision grid has \(N=HW/p^2\) patches. A 2 by 2 merger gives \(N/4\) visual decoder tokens when both grid dimensions are even.

Doubling both image dimensions quadruples patch count. Dense vision attention score entries grow sixteenfold; projections grow fourfold. Decoder attention instead depends on the total visual plus text length.
Attention score counts are not measured latency or peak memory. Fused attention can avoid storing the full score matrix; decoder KV state grows linearly with its sequence length.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, count a 224 by 224 image with patch width 14: 256 vision patches, 64 visual tokens after 2 by 2 merging, and 66 positions including two delimiters. For a 448 by 448 input, get 1024, 256 and 258 respectively. With 32 text tokens and no other special tokens, the decoder lengths are 98 and 290. Implement the TensorTonic rectangular patch contract and check its channel ordering against a nested-loop oracle on CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1.
traps: Counting a pooled CLIP embedding as a sequence of patch features. A pooled vector discards the explicit grid the projector may need.
Changing a frozen encoder's input resolution without checking its positional encoding and preprocessing contract. A valid tensor shape is not proof of compatible features.
Calling a sixteenfold attention-score increase a sixteenfold runtime increase. Other operations, kernels and memory traffic still matter.

selfTest.q: Why does Qwen2-VL describe 66 tokens for a 224 by 224 image?
selfTest.a: Patch width 14 gives 256 patches. Merging each 2 by 2 group gives 64 visual tokens; the start and end delimiters add two positions.

selfTest.q: Does doubling image resolution quadruple the whole decoder's attention cost?
selfTest.a: No. Visual token count quadruples under the stated grid rule, but dense decoder attention uses the square of text plus visual length, including delimiters.

selfTest.q: Can a center crop improve efficiency without changing the task?
selfTest.a: Only if it preserves the evidence the task needs. Cropping away a small object or text changes what can be answered from the input.

units.title: Projectors between representation spaces, and early, late and cross-attention fusion
outcomes: Trace visual features through a linear or MLP projector into decoder-width embeddings.
Compare joint token processing, separate-encoder scoring and inserted cross-attention using explicit interaction shapes.
Test a gated fusion branch against the unfused residual path at initialization.
units.why: Equal widths permit concatenation, but do not establish semantic alignment. Fusion placement also determines which representations can interact and what a text-only control must bypass.

study.locator: Sections 3.1.1 to 3.1.3, Figures 4 to 6: resampler, gated cross-attention and image-causal masking
study.depth: These are the architecture sections in this edition; Sections 2.1 to 2.3 are related work. Do not implement the full model.

study.title: Modern LLM Notebook 29: projector and fusion
study.locator: Sections 5 and 6, then Exercise 2: Implement a Single-Layer Projector
study.depth: The Section 6 demo adds LayerNorm after the gated residual, so its zero gate returns normalized input, not unchanged input. Use Flamingo Figure 5 for an identity-preserving insertion.

focus: For visual features of shape \(B	imes N	imes d_v\), a biased linear projector has \(d_vd_l+d_l\) parameters and returns \(B	imes N	imes d_l\). It changes width, not token count.

Use early fusion to mean joint processing of modality tokens; Chameleon uses it from pretraining. Separate CLIP towers combine only at scoring, a late interaction. LLaVA concatenates pretrained features before decoder processing. State the actual interaction rather than relying on labels alone.

Cross-attention uses text queries and visual keys and values: per-head score shape \(B	imes h	imes T	imes N\). Its cost includes text self-attention, visual encoding, projections and any resampler, not just this matrix.
For a finite branch output, \(x+	anh(\alpha)f(x,v)\) equals \(x\) at a zero gate. This is an initialization contract, not evidence that the model later uses vision.
units.reproduce: On CPU with PyTorch 2.14.1, build biased linear and two-layer GELU projectors from width 32 to 64, with hidden width 64. Count 2112 and 6272 parameters and verify both map `(2, 6, 32)` to `(2, 6, 64)`. Implement the gated residual from Flamingo Figure 5 and test zero-gate identity on finite inputs. Contrast it with the notebook's post-residual normalization.
traps: Treating equal embedding dimensions as aligned spaces. Only an objective and external evaluation can establish useful correspondence.
Claiming a resampler removes all resolution cost. Its output length is fixed, but visual encoding and resampling still process the input grid.
Treating the notebook's schematic attention-entry counts as total FLOPs or a speed measurement. They omit projections and the vision tower.

selfTest.q: Does a tokenwise MLP projector reduce a 196-token grid to 32 tokens?
selfTest.a: No. It changes each token's features independently. Pooling, merging or a query-based resampler must explicitly change the token axis.

selfTest.q: Why can Flamingo text depend on older images when direct cross-attention sees only the most recent image?
selfTest.a: Earlier text states can already contain information from those images. Causal text self-attention carries that information forward.

selfTest.q: At a zero gate, must the added branch's own parameters receive nonzero gradients?
selfTest.a: No. Their gradient through the gated output is multiplied by zero. The gate can receive a gradient and open the branch on later updates.
